questions.q: Without branch protection, what can a developer still do even when the ci.yml workflow shows a red X on their pull request?
options: The pull request is automatically closed after 24 hours
Click Merge anyway — the workflow informs, but on its own it doesn't yet block anything
Only a repository admin can merge a failing pull request
Nothing — GitHub automatically prevents any merge when a workflow fails
questions.explain: A workflow running (even failing) is just information until a branch protection rule is configured to require it before merging.

questions.q: What is the specific GitHub setting that turns the CI workflow from a report into a real gate?
options: Setting the repository to private instead of public
Enabling two-factor authentication on the repository
Adding a CODEOWNERS file to the repository
A branch protection rule for main with "Require status checks to pass before merging," selecting the build-and-test job specifically
questions.explain: Required status checks are what disable the Merge button until the named job passes — the actual mechanism that blocks a bad merge.

questions.q: Once this branch protection rule is active, what does a pull request with a failing build-and-test check look like to a developer?
options: The pull request is deleted automatically
An email is sent to the repository owner, but the PR still merges normally
A red X next to build-and-test and a disabled Merge button, with GitHub's own message that required checks haven't passed
Identical to a passing one, with no visible difference
questions.explain: GitHub visibly disables the merge button and explains why, linking directly into the failing run's log.

questions.q: Why does this lesson call the required status check "the last link" connecting Chapter 4's tests to a real governance outcome?
options: Because a test running automatically only matters if its result can actually stop a merge — without the required check, a developer could see a failure and still merge anyway
Because Chapter 4's tests only run after this setting is configured
Because it replaces the need for any tests at all
Because it's unrelated to the tests built in Chapter 4
questions.explain: Tests plus an automatically-running workflow still don't block anything on their own — the required status check is what makes the block real.

questions.q: How does fixing a failing check and pushing a new commit affect the blocked pull request?
options: Nothing changes; a human must manually re-enable the Merge button
The repository owner must manually approve the fix before CI will run again
The workflow re-triggers automatically, and the Merge button re-enables the moment the check passes
A brand-new pull request must be opened from scratch
questions.explain: A new commit to the same PR automatically re-runs the required check, and the merge button re-enables as soon as it goes green.
